Specific_Friction: HR teams managing performance and compensation cycles via spreadsheet world have no self-service mechanism for complex questions — creating a single-person knowledge bottleneck that makes the entire organization vulnerable. When one HR leader holds all the knowledge of how to handle edge cases (mid-cycle deactivations, comp statement sharing, manager-on-leave review packets), every question from every team member requires that person's time. New HRBP onboarding takes months because there's no searchable institutional knowledge — just one person's memory. 'I don't know how we would have gotten through that period of time if I couldn't have just self-served' — the realization that spreadsheet-era HR is a single point of failure for entire people operations.
Severity/Impact: High. HR knowledge bottleneck at mid-market SaaS. Named exec: Lisa DeCamp (Director of People Operations), Peaksware. Quantified: 270 employees managed via spreadsheets before migration; dozens of AI-answered complex questions during critical compensation cycle; new HRBP onboarded without training (hasn't come to me with any questions); real-time visibility into performance and compensation data. Quote: 'The ability to use it as a thought partner, to say, I don't even know how to go about doing this, what ideas do you have? That was huge.'

Specific_Friction: Organizations running annual surveys with manual feedback processes (screenshot → crop → paste into PowerPoint) have no continuous feedback loop — making employee listening a once-a-year event that produces reports no one acts on. Without a closed loop between survey and action, employees learn their feedback changes nothing and stop responding. 'Without a continuous feedback loop, you're just shouting in the dark.' The manual process also means insights take so long to produce that they're stale by the time teams see them — losing the window to act on what employees actually said.
Severity/Impact: High. HR engagement transformation at global media brand. Named exec: Stephanie Lunn (Global People & Culture Director), Guinness World Records. Quantified: 6 hours saved per survey cycle; 90% peak engagement survey participation; 76% adjudicator participation (freelancers); 510 comments across surveys; 61% onboarding completion; decision-making scores improved after action loop closed; 70-year-old brand with offices in London, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai, Americas. Quote: 'I was screenshotting, putting the screenshot into Paint, cropping it, and then putting it back into PowerPoint. It was easily an extra day's work. Now I can enjoy my weekend.' 'Without a continuous feedback loop, you're just shouting in the dark.'
